sections: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

blocks.text: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models
blocks.section: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

blocks.text: We investigate two complementary strategies for adapting GR00T 2. Direct GR00T 2 post-training updates the pretrained model through RL or self-imitation, while residual RL freezes GR00T 2 and learns a lightweight corrective policy. The former improves the underlying generative policy, whereas the latter targets precisioncritical stages where GR00T 2 already produces approximately correct behaviors.
blocks.section: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

blocks.text: F.1.1. Direct GR00T 2 Post-Training
blocks.section: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

blocks.text: Stochastic Exploration with CPS. To enable exploration and likelihood-based policy optimization (Liu et al., 2025; Lei et al., 2026), we replace GR00T 2’s deterministic Euler action updates with Coefficients-Preserving Sampling (CPS) (Wang and Yu, 2025) during rollout. Noise is injected only into the action denoising process. Video denoising remains deterministic given its initial latent, while video features continue to condition action generation.
blocks.section: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

blocks.text: Following DPPO (Ren et al., 2025) and RL-100 (Lei et al., 2026), we optimize GR00T 2 through its action denoising process. Let 𝑡index environment decisions and 𝑘index action-denoising events. GR00T 2 uses four such events: joint passes (𝑘= 0, 2) update video and action latents through a shared DiT, while cached passes (𝑘= 1, 3) update action tokens using video and state keys and values from the preceding joint pass (Fig. 46).

blocks.text: Online RL with GRPO. We optimize GR00T 2 from its own successful and failed rollouts with a GRPO-style algorithm developed through AutoRL (Sec. F.2). A training round collects 𝑁𝑔attempts for each selected reset context 𝑔(a task paired with a scene layout) under a fixed behavior policy. Attempt 𝑖of context 𝑔receives a binary return 𝑅𝑔,𝑖∈{0, 1}.

blocks.text: Persistent context table. The historical means 𝑚𝑔live in a global table indexed by context. The table persists across rounds and, through checkpointing, across training segments, so it records how well the policy has done in every context so far. Once a round’s advantages have been computed, each visited context is updated by an exponential moving average of its round mean, with 𝛼EMA = 0.25 and 𝑚𝑔= 𝜇𝑔on the first visit. Unvisited contexts are left untouched. Updating the table after advantage computation ensures that the historical term uses only preceding rounds.
blocks.section: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

blocks.text: Clipped transition-level objective for a denoising policy. GR00T 2 produces actions by iterative denoising, so the exact action log-likelihood that GRPO would compare between policies is not available. CPS, however, gives a Gaussian density for every action-denoising transition, and we score the policy on those transitions instead. On the selected joint denoising events 𝒦= {0, 2} we maximize the clipped surrogate (Liu et al., 2025; Lei et al., 2026; Schulman et al., 2017)
blocks.section: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

blocks.text: 𝑟𝑔,𝑖,𝑡,𝑘ˆ𝐴𝑔,𝑖,𝑡, clip(𝑟𝑔,𝑖,𝑡,𝑘, 1 −𝜖clip, 1 + 𝜖clip) ˆ𝐴𝑔,𝑖,𝑡 min where ℬis the batch of recorded decisions, 𝜖clip is the clipping threshold, and 𝑟= exp(ℓ𝜃−ℓold) is the current-tobehavior likelihood ratio for one recorded transition. Gaussian log densities condition on the observation context and input action latent at event 𝑘and sum over executed coordinates. Ratios are not multiplied across events or decisions. In practice, rather than sampling 𝑘, each minibatch scores one joint event, alternating between 𝑘= 0 and 𝑘= 2. Recorded action latents are teacher-forced, while video computation is reconstructed under the current parameters. Gradients flow through the selected joint pass, including the shared DiT, state/action encoders, and action decoder. Carried latents are detached, yielding a local surrogate without backpropagation through the full denoising chain.

blocks.text: GRPO-Induced Self-Imitation. Online RL enables GR00T 2 to discover successful behaviors through exploration, while supervised learning provides a potentially more stable optimization approach for consolidating these behaviors. We investigate GRPO-induced self-imitation, combining the exploration capabilities of RL with the optimization stability of supervised fine-tuning.
blocks.section: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

blocks.text: Task success determines which trajectories are selected, while the learning signal comes from the original video and action supervision. This enables GR00T 2 to benefit from RL-discovered successful behaviors while optimizing a standard supervised objective, without additional robot rollouts, demonstrations, or human corrective actions.

blocks.text: F.1.2. Residual Reinforcement Learning
blocks.section: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

blocks.text: Direct GR00T 2 post-training updates the generative policy itself. A complementary approach is to retain GR00T 2’s pretrained capabilities and learn targeted corrections for precision-critical stages, where approximately correct trajectories can still fail because of small alignment or contact errors.
blocks.section: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

blocks.text: We keep GR00T 2 frozen and train a lightweight residual policy to correct its actions online. Unlike direct GR00T 2 training, residual RL does not use CPS. Instead, it relies on the stochastic residual actor for exploration.
blocks.section: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

blocks.text: The residual operates within designated task stages. At each decision 𝑗, a tanh-squashed Gaussian actor 𝜋𝜑 receives observations z𝑗comprising camera images, proprioception, GR00T 2’s forecast end-effector targets, and the current correction offset. The actor produces a bounded residual action a𝑗over the next control horizon.
blocks.section: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

The operator ⊕composes the correction offset with GR00T 2’s end-effector target. Zero residual action leaves the current offset unchanged, while zero offset recovers the base policy.
blocks.section: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

blocks.text: Following HIL-SERL (Luo et al., 2025), we train the residual actor using Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) (Haarnoja et al., 2018) with prior demonstrations and online interaction, including occasional human corrections. Evaluation episodes are manually scored using binary task-specific success criteria.
blocks.section: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

blocks.text: We draw half of each critic batch from online data and half from demonstrations, and train an ensemble of critics using bootstrapped returns. The actor objective combines entropy-regularized policy improvement with a zero-residual prior and imitation of successful residual actions:

The entropy coefficient 𝛼controls exploration, while 𝜆𝑄, 𝜆0, and 𝜆bc weight the critic, zero-residual regularization, and behavior-cloning terms, respectively.
blocks.section: F.1. RL-Based Adaptation of World-Action Models

blocks.text: The zero-residual prior discourages unnecessary corrections, while successful experience reinforces effective behavior. Residual RL thus enables targeted adaptation without modifying pretrained GR00T 2 weights.
